description:
## Outcome

Trusted built-in extensions can register replaceable tools, commands, providers, policy advice, context contributions, namespaced session state, and namespaced result data through one Jidoka host.

## Why now

The host mechanism must be stable before optional extensions or default coding tools appear. It must keep policy authoritative and sessions portable.

## Current state

Jidoka has operation sources, provider capabilities, controls, and events as separate mechanisms. It has no host that resolves a registration, scopes extension state, dispatches lifecycle events, or prevents namespace collision. Default tools are absent.

## Ownership and boundary

This is a `jidoka` kernel change. Built-in factories are trusted injected host code. Agent data selects IDs only. The host composes existing public operation and provider contracts. It cannot bypass the policy gate or write to CLI stdout.

## Detailed implementation

1. Add a public `Jidoka.Extension.Host` contract that opens resolved bindings for a session and closes them on terminal paths.
2. Define registration slots for tools, deterministic commands, providers, advisory policy, pre-turn context, lifecycle handlers, namespaced state, and namespaced result fields.
3. Define collision and replacement rules. A trusted host setting can replace or disable a default registration by stable ID. Agent data cannot override trust.
4. Route tools through `Jidoka.Operation.Source` and the policy gate. Route providers through the existing model capability contract.
5. Validate and checkpoint namespaced JSON state at safe session points. Keep live extension instance data only in runtime context.
6. Isolate handler failures and return stable extension errors.
7. Project only namespaced, registered result data.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fake built-in extension registers and uses each supported slot through public contracts.
- [ ] A host can disable or replace one default tool by ID.
- [ ] Duplicate unapproved IDs and state/result namespace collisions fail before a turn.
- [ ] Every external action still passes the authoritative policy gate.
- [ ] Portable namespaced state survives resume and fork; live instance data does not.
- [ ] Handler failure gives stable error evidence and always closes the extension instance.

## Test plan

- Success: fake extension adds context, one tool, one lifecycle handler, state, and result field.
- Invalid input: collision, unknown slot, malformed state/result data, and mode mismatch.
- Runtime failure: handler, provider, tool, checkpoint, and close failures.
- Boundary and security: extension advisory allow cannot override host deny; result namespace cannot replace core JSON fields.
- Deterministic capability: fake host registry, extension, LLM, policy, store, clock, and IDs.
- JSONL and exit status: projected extension result data is JSON-safe and namespaced; no direct output occurs.

## Documentation

Add an extension-host author guide for built-ins. Define slots, order, replacement, state, result namespace, policy, and failure rules.

## Non-goals

Do not start external processes. Do not add installation, hot reload, MCP, custom TUI, subagents, or a marketplace.

## Dependencies

Blocking issues:

- `jido_cli-tqg.4.3` — Emit versioned portable extension lifecycle events
- `jido_cli-tqg.3.1` — Gate every external effect with authoritative host policy

Features unlocked by this story:

- Language-neutral process extensions
- The removable default coding pack
- One extension path for interactive and automation modes

## Commit plan

Create exactly one focused `jidoka` commit. Use a message such as `feat(jidoka): add the built-in extension host (jido_cli-tqg.4.4)`. Do not include another backlog feature.

## Verification commands

```sh
cd /Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_cli/jidoka
mix test test/jidoka/extension/host_test.exs test/integration/extension_host_integration_test.exs test/jidoka/operation_source_test.exs
mix quality
mix test
mix docs
```
title: Add the built-in Jidoka extension host
